lines.en: It is a basic principle that everyone is innocent until proven guilty.
The new law is expected to reduce corruption, although some doubt it will be enforced.
What the victim wanted was not revenge, but simply to be heard.
Not until the evidence was presented in court did the public understand the whole story.
However strict the law may be, it means little if it is not applied equally to everyone.
The judge is said to have taken three days to reach her decision.
Were the punishment always to fit the crime, fewer people would lose faith in the system.
It is better to let a guilty person go free than to punish an innocent one, or so the old principle says.
Little attention was paid to his objection, even though it later proved to be correct.
What makes a society just is not the number of its laws, but the fairness with which they are applied.
It is not the harshness of a sentence but the certainty of being caught that discourages crime.
Were witnesses not afraid to speak, many more crimes would be solved.
The lawyer is reported to have refused the case because she doubted her client's story.
What troubles many people is not the law itself, but how slowly the courts apply it.
Hardly had the verdict been read when the crowd outside began to cheer.
